objective_for_doctor: A 17-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have feeling nauseous or do you feel like vomiting, significant dyspnea, and did your cheeks suddenly turn red.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. I’m feeling really nauseous and like I might vomit, and I’m having significant trouble breathing. My cheeks suddenly turned pink/red, and I have a rash with itching (about 6/10) on different areas, including my right biceps, around my mouth, on my throat/thyroid cartilage area, and both my right and left ankles.

Dr. Agent: Let’s quickly clarify—did this start suddenly within minutes to an hour after a new food/medication (especially NSAIDs like ibuprofen), insect sting, or latex exposure, and do you have wheezing/voice hoarseness or lip/tongue swelling?  
Dr. Agent: Also, are you feeling lightheaded/faint, and have you taken anything so far (antihistamine/epinephrine)?

It started pretty suddenly after I ate something—dark-fleshed fish or Swiss cheese—right before the reaction. I don’t know about wheezing or voice hoarseness, and I haven’t noticed lip or tongue swelling. I feel a bit nauseous but I’m not lightheaded/faint, and I haven’t taken anything yet.

Doctor: Do you have any hives or raised welts that move around, and how quickly did the rash and breathing symptoms start after eating (minutes vs >1 hour)?  
Doctor: Also—any stomach cramps/diarrhea, fever, or new medications/supplements in the last week?

Yes, it’s a rash with pink redness and some spots are bigger than 1 cm, but I can’t say if they “move around.” It started within minutes to an hour after eating the dark-fleshed fish or Swiss cheese. I don’t have fever, and I don’t have diarrhea or stomach cramps that I can tell; I also haven’t started any new medications or supplements in the last week.

Doctor: This sounds like a possible **anaphylaxis or acute allergic reaction** triggered by that food—did you have **any lip/eyelid swelling**, **throat tightness**, **wheezing or coughing**, or **faster heartbeat**?  
Doctor: If you have a pulse oximeter, what is your **current SpO₂**—and do you feel worse when lying down?

I haven’t noticed lip or eyelid swelling, and I haven’t noticed throat tightness, wheezing, or coughing. I don’t have a pulse oximeter, and I can’t say about a faster heartbeat or worse when lying down—I just feel very short of breath and nauseous.

Doctor: This is still concerning for a food-triggered severe allergic reaction—right now I need to know: can you speak in full sentences, and do you have any visible swelling of the throat/neck or a “tight” voice?  
Doctor: Also, do you have any history of asthma or previous anaphylaxis, and are you currently on any beta-blocker medications (for heart problems)?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry_now + Vital_Signs (HR/BP/RR/Temp)

I can speak in full sentences, and I don’t feel like my voice is tight or hoarse. I don’t know about visible throat/neck swelling from the outside, but I do have rash redness around my throat/thyroid cartilage area. I don’t have a history of asthma or previous anaphylaxis that I know of, and I’m not on any beta-blocker medications. I’m not able to do pulse oximetry or my own vitals right now.

Doctor: Given onset within minutes to an hour after food plus dyspnea and diffuse itchy rash near the throat, I’m treating this as **high-risk anaphylaxis even without wheeze/hoarseness**—do you have an epinephrine auto-injector available at home or with you?  
Doctor: Also, are you having any **worsening** shortness of breath, **lightheadedness**, or vomiting/abdominal cramping right now?

I don’t have an epinephrine auto-injector with me. Right now my shortness of breath feels significant, but I don’t feel lightheaded/faint, and I’m not vomiting or having strong abdominal cramping that I can tell.

Dr. Agent: I’m concerned for **anaphylaxis** triggered by food (rapid onset within minutes–1 hour, itchy rash with throat/neck involvement, significant dyspnea) even though you don’t feel faint or have vomiting. Do you have someone who can take you **to the ER/Call emergency services now**, and can you do a quick check for any **lip/tongue swelling** or **voice change** at this moment?  
Dr. Agent: Also, if you can access it, are you willing to take an over-the-counter antihistamine **(cetirizine/loratadine)** while waiting—but **you need emergency care urgently because you don’t have epinephrine**.

DIAGNOSIS READY: High-risk food-triggered anaphylaxis (acute systemic allergic reaction) — requires immediate emergency treatment.
